01 · Load the stencil

Place the stencil (up to 750 × 750 × 40 mm) in the chamber; set the cleaning parameters.

02 · Spray clean

Four fixed spray rods spray aqueous cleaning liquid while the stencil moves forwards and backwards by motor.

03 · DI rinse

Four fixed spray bars rinse with DI water; real-time 1 µm filtration keeps solder paste balls out.

04 · Hot-air dry

Four hot-air blades dry the stencil; a 5.5 HP blower shortens dry time.

The hidden cost of manual stencil cleaning

Blocked apertures and wasted liquid are taxing your line

Every stencil with residue and every drop of wasted cleaning liquid costs money. An electric stencil cleaner changes that math.

Solder paste balls return

Without real-time filtration, solder paste balls wash back onto the stencil and re-contaminate boards.

Blocked apertures

Residue in stencil apertures causes paste misprint and rework.

Soft hoses wear out

Bending liquid and air hoses on moving spray heads fail and leak frequently.

Long dry times

Weak drying slows the stencil changeover between jobs.

Plastic pipes contaminate

Plastic liquid pipes risk contamination and corrosion in cleaning chemistry.

Manual results vary

Hand-cleaning quality depends on the operator, batch and shift.

SME800 specifications

From the SME800 brochure (2021)
Stencil size750 mm (L) × 750 mm (W) × 40 mm (H) maximum
Cleaning agentAqueous cleaning liquid for cleaning; DI or DM water for rinsing
Tank capacity60 L maximum (liquid tank and water tank)
Way of cleaning4 fixed spraying rods spray liquid; the stencil moves forwards and backwards by motor
Way of rinsing4 fixed spraying bars spray DI water; stencil moves forwards and backwards
Way of drying4 hot-air blades blow hot air; 5.5 HP hot-air blower for frequent start and stop
Filter grade1 µm for cleaning, 1 µm for DI water (real-time filtering)
DI water supplyOpen-loop 30–60 L/min (≤ 0.4 MPa); closed-loop cyclic with conductivity-based discharge
Electric pump4 HP stainless steel pump
Fluid pathTotal SUS304 liquid pipes with angle valves, no plastic hose
ElectricsMitsui PLC, touch panel, inverter and breakers; Schneider relays and contactors; Omron switching power supply
ApplicationsSolder paste stencils, red glue stencils, resin / copper masks, misprint PCB cleaning

Installation guide

Install and commission the SME800

Reference procedure for an electric stencil cleaner. Full documentation ships with the machine.

01 · Site preparation

Place the machine on a solid, flat, clean floor with enough space for installation, spare parts and maintenance.

02 · Utilities

Connect power per the nameplate, DI water supply (30–60 L/min open loop reference) and drainage; connect the exhaust vent.

03 · Liquid & filters

Fill the cleaning liquid and water tanks; check the 1 µm filters for cleaning and DI water.

04 · Pre-run check

Check spray rods, air blades, pumps and valves; confirm the stencil transport moves freely.

05 · Clean test

Load a stencil, set the cleaning parameters, press start and verify the clean-rinse-dry result.

Technical evaluation FAQ

Questions buyers ask before ordering

What does the SME800 clean?

Solder paste stencils, red glue stencils, resin and copper masks, and misprint PCBs, using aqueous cleaning liquid followed by a DI water rinse.

How does the cleaning process work?

The stencil moves forwards and backwards by motor while four fixed spray rods spray aqueous liquid, then four fixed bars rinse with DI water, then four hot-air blades dry it.

What size stencils fit?

Stencils up to 750 mm (L) × 750 mm (W) × 40 mm (H) are supported.

How is contamination prevented?

Real-time 1 µm filtration on both the cleaning liquid and DI water keeps solder paste balls from returning to the stencil and re-contaminating boards.

Why is drying fast?

A 5.5 HP hot-air blower with four air blades delivers a high air rate, greatly reducing dry time between jobs.

How do I get a price and delivery time?

Email info@smthelp.com or WhatsApp +86 136 0256 2576 with your stencil types, cleaning liquid and volume. Quotation and delivery schedule are provided after technical confirmation — typically the same working day.
